hunks.baseline: If the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families showed up like clockwork in those stories, then the imperial court had the East Depot, which stood alongside the Embroidered Uniform Guard as its other great power.
hunks.sol: If the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families showed up like clockwork in those stories, the imperial court had the East Depot alongside the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

hunks.baseline: And Hong Jin was a member of that very East Depot.
hunks.sol: And Hong Jin had been a member of that very East Depot.

hunks.baseline: “……Is there a fake East Depot, then?”
hunks.sol: “…Is there a fake East Depot, then?”

hunks.baseline: The endless incidents and disasters in Murim kept me busy enough. Who would’ve expected to suddenly get tangled up with the imperial court like this?
hunks.sol: The endless incidents and disasters in Murim kept me busy enough. Who would’ve expected to get tangled up with the imperial court like this?

hunks.baseline: *Still, if Hong Jin really did come from the East Depot, then some of the things he’s shown me make a lot more sense.*
hunks.sol: *Still, if Hong Jin came from the East Depot, that would explain a lot about him.*

hunks.baseline: Newly astonished, I looked at Hong Jin.
hunks.sol: I looked at Hong Jin with fresh astonishment.

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin must have had a similar thought. He’d been glancing sideways at Hong Jin, and now he whispered in a voice barely above a breath.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin must have had a similar thought. He glanced sideways at Hong Jin and whispered in a voice barely above a breath.

hunks.baseline: “……Please, just shut your mouth.”
hunks.sol: “…Please, just shut your mouth.”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin was facedown, wailing like a Communist Party member caught in an ideological purge and dragged off to the Aoji coal mines. hunks.baseline: Very sadly, Hong Jin was right.
hunks.sol: Sadly enough, Hong Jin was right.

hunks.baseline: The Embroidered Uniform Guards were staring at us like they couldn’t believe what a bunch of idiots we were. Prince Shangshan, who’d just woken up and was still groggy, had his eyes wide as he asked me,

hunks.baseline: I held my tongue to protect the young prince’s innocence. Just then, a group of people came down the endless staircase—long enough to make me wonder if it had been built to torture subjects—and stopped in front of us.
hunks.sol: I held my tongue to protect the young prince’s innocence. Just then, a group came down the endless staircase—long enough to make me wonder if it had been built to torture subjects—and stopped in front of us.

hunks.baseline: They wore official robes made of black silk, and their ages varied widely.
Some looked barely twenty, at most; others were old men with deeply wrinkled faces.
hunks.sol: They wore official robes of black silk, but ranged in age from young men who looked barely twenty to old men with deeply wrinkled faces.

hunks.baseline: But their robes weren’t the only thing they had in common. I realized at once.
hunks.sol: Their robes weren’t the only thing they had in common. I realized at once.

hunks.baseline: Every one of them had a face powdered white and lips painted red. Their voices were neither a woman’s nor a man’s, and their small frames showed even through the loose fit of their robes.
hunks.sol: Every one of them had a face powdered white and lips painted red. Their voices sounded neither like women’s nor men’s, and even their loose robes couldn’t hide their small frames.

hunks.baseline: There was more to people than what you could see.
hunks.sol: What you saw wasn’t everything.

hunks.baseline: I could feel the immense energy coiled inside their small frames. At the same time, I recalled the name of the organization I’d just heard.
hunks.sol: I could feel the immense qi coiled inside their small frames. At the same time, I recalled the name of the organization I’d just heard.

hunks.baseline: Though there was a considerable age difference between them, Hong Jin spoke to him casually and without deference.
hunks.sol: Despite the considerable age difference between them, Hong Jin spoke to him without a hint of deference.

hunks.baseline: That meant Hong Jin’s position back then must have been quite high. The old eunuch’s wrinkles deepened further.
hunks.sol: That meant Hong Jin’s position back then must have been quite high. The old eunuch’s wrinkles deepened.

hunks.baseline: Hong Jin continued in a clear voice.
hunks.sol: Hong Jin’s voice rang clear.

hunks.baseline: Hong Jin’s words had a hard edge beneath them, and the air around us froze.
hunks.sol: The barb in Hong Jin’s words left the air around us icy.

hunks.baseline: Hong Jin had alluded to that fact, and the reaction of the Embroidered Uniform Guards and the East Depot eunuchs—the Son of Heaven’s own hands and feet—was settled from the start.
hunks.sol: Hong Jin had alluded to that fact, and the reaction of the Embroidered Uniform Guards and the East Depot eunuchs—the Son of Heaven’s own hands and feet—had been inevitable from the start.

hunks.baseline: In time that seemed to pass slowly, I reached out and pressed down on the hand of someone gripping a sword hilt tightly.
hunks.sol: In time that seemed to pass slowly, I reached out and pressed down on the hand gripping a sword hilt.

hunks.baseline: To send the blade, not even halfway drawn, back where it belonged.
hunks.sol: The blade, not even halfway drawn, slid back where it belonged.

hunks.baseline: But I didn’t bother answering, nor did I knock down my opponent, who’d already gone rigid as a statue.
hunks.sol: But I didn’t bother answering, nor did I knock down the man who’d already gone rigid as a statue.

hunks.baseline: The wind, catching up with my figure after it had moved like a flash of light, whipped in every direction.
hunks.sol: The wind, catching up with me after I’d moved like a flash of light, whipped in every direction.

hunks.baseline: When had he—
hunks.sol: *When did he get there?*

hunks.baseline: There was no denying the distance between us was considerable, but the fact that I hadn’t sensed him was proof that the middle-aged man’s martial prowess was no less than mine.
hunks.sol: There was no denying the distance between us was considerable. But the fact that I hadn’t sensed him proved the middle-aged man’s martial prowess was no less than mine.

hunks.baseline: I fixed my gaze on the man, feeling my mind grow cold.
hunks.sol: My thoughts turned cold as I watched him.

hunks.baseline: Instead of using lightness skill, he came slowly down the stairs with the leisurely gait of a carefree man. He smiled at me and spoke.
hunks.sol: Instead of using lightness skill, he came slowly down the stairs with the leisurely gait of a man out for a stroll. He smiled at me and spoke.

hunks.baseline: Even if he hadn’t been wearing a gleaming golden suit of armor, the shout that rang out the next moment would’ve told me.
hunks.sol: Even if he hadn’t been wearing gleaming golden armor, the shout that rang out the next moment would’ve told me.

hunks.baseline: So was the middle-aged man approaching through a sea of flashing gold.
hunks.sol: So was the middle-aged man approaching through that sea of flashing gold.

hunks.baseline: “I, Baek Yeon, Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, pay my respects to His Highness Prince Shangshan. I serve only the Emperor with my utmost loyalty, so please forgive me for being unable to kneel, with a heart as vast as the sea.”
hunks.sol: “I, Baek Yeon, Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, pay my respects to His Highness Prince Shangshan. I serve only the Emperor with my utmost loyalty, so I ask you to forgive me, with a heart as vast as the sea, for not kneeling.”

hunks.baseline: Still, he held the post of Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard for a reason. He was the Son of Heaven’s most trusted military officer, and the head of a force even the highest-ranking officials feared.
hunks.sol: Still, the post of Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard carried that kind of power. He was the Son of Heaven’s most trusted military officer and the head of a force even the highest-ranking officials feared.

hunks.baseline: He was telling us to put an end to this here and now.
hunks.sol: He was telling us to end the matter here and now.

hunks.sol: Hong Jin stared at the middle-aged man—or rather, Baek Yeon, Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard—with a deeply restrained gaze, then leaned toward Prince Shangshan and whispered,

hunks.sol: Intervening when an Embroidered Uniform Guard drew his sword had been proper for me as the prince’s guard in name. But from here on, it was best to follow Hong Jin’s lead.

hunks.baseline: “That is precisely what I want. This is an order from your prince.”
hunks.sol: “That is precisely what I want. This is a royal command.”
